chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluyah (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Harun ibn Muslim, from Mus'ada ibn Ziyad, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from Ali (peace be upon them) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Shyness is upon two faces; from it is weakness, and from it is strength, and Islam, and faith.'
ai.seo_question: What are the two types of shyness mentioned in this hadith?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq to distinguish between *haya' al-dha'f* (shyness from inadequacy or timidity) and *haya' al-quwwah* (shyness as a virtue rooted in faith). This dual classification highlights how modesty serves as both a psychological state and a spiritual pillar, reinforcing the Shia emphasis on *haya'* as an essential component of *Iman* (faith) and moral integrity.
